items.headline: OpenAI acquires Ona, the rebranded Gitpod, to give Codex agents persistent cloud sandboxes
items.diff_narrative: This extends the agent-execution thread that on 2026-06-11 was anchored by Simon Willison's datasette-agent 0.2a0 and its durable, restart-surviving suspended conversations - state that holds across a process restart. Where yesterday the durability primitive was built in the open at the individual-tool level, today the same need is consolidated by acquisition: OpenAI announced on June 11 it is buying Ona (the German startup formerly known as Gitpod) and folding it into the Codex group, because Ona runs coding agents inside persistent cloud sandboxes so a multi-day task keeps executing after the developer's laptop is powered off. The delta versus June 11 is the move up a layer and a shift in framing - from an open-source toolkit adding human-in-the-loop checkpoints to a frontier lab buying the durable off-machine substrate outright, explicitly to contest the enterprise coding workflow that European trade coverage frames as Anthropic's stronghold.

items.headline: Zyphra open-sources Zamba2-VL, a 1.2B/2.7B/7B Mamba2-Transformer hybrid vision-language family
items.diff_narrative: A net-new open-model storyline with no antecedent on 2026-06-11, whose open-weight lead was Google's DiffusionGemma - a 26B text-diffusion model that swaps autoregressive decoding for parallel block refinement. Today's release is a different architecture answering a different problem: Zyphra's June 12 Zamba2-VL pairs Mamba2 state-space layers with a few shared transformer blocks and reuses the Qwen2.5-VL vision encoder, cutting time-to-first-token by roughly an order of magnitude on 32K-token prefill while the small models post strong perception scores (the 2.7B hits PixMoCount 82.5 and DocVQA 90.9; the 1.2B nearly doubles InternVL3.5-1B on visual counting). Where June 11's open release was about faster text generation via a new decoding paradigm, today's is about fast, fully-licensed multimodal perception at the 1-7B sizes that fit on local hardware. It appears for the first time today, so there is no prior-day version to diff against.

items.headline: Moonshot ships Kimi Work, a downloadable desktop agent running a 300-sub-agent swarm on Kimi K2.6
items.diff_narrative: This continues the agent-deployment thread from 2026-06-11's datasette-agent durable-checkpoint item, but pulls it toward the opposite pole. Moonshot launched Kimi Work on June 12 as a downloadable desktop app (macOS on Apple silicon and Windows) that acts directly on the user's machine - coordinating an Agent Swarm of about 300 parallel sub-agents, driving the logged-in browser through a WebBridge extension, and firing scheduled jobs via a built-in cron engine with a keep-awake toggle - on the open-weight Kimi K2.6 (about 32B active per token, 256K context), the same weights Unsloth already serves on-device via a 2-bit (UD-Q2_K_XL) dynamic-quantization build. The delta versus June 11 is that the long-horizon-autonomy question yesterday's open toolkit raised now splits into two competing answers landing the same day: persistent off-machine sandboxes (OpenAI/Ona) versus an always-on local swarm operating on the user's own files and browser session (Kimi Work) - both betting on durable autonomy but disagreeing on where the agent should live.

items.headline: The AI-lab IPO race goes concrete as SpaceX prices the largest IPO ever and OpenAI opens an Oracle-credits path
items.diff_narrative: This is where the markets/corporate-activity thread moves after 2026-06-11, which tracked the semiconductor complex - Intel +8.5% and Micron +9% on June 8 snapping back from the Broadcom-driven washout, with leadership rotating toward US foundry capacity. Today the same capital-markets lens shifts off the chip tape and onto the labs' path to public markets: Anthropic's confidential June 1 Form S-1 (on its $65B round at a $965B post-money and a run-rate past $47B) and OpenAI's own listing preparation set the two largest labs on a collision course, and the backdrop turned concrete on June 11 when SpaceX priced 555.6 million shares at $135 to raise about $75B - the largest IPO in history, eclipsing Saudi Aramco - resetting the ceiling for how much the public market will absorb for one high-multiple name. Alongside, OpenAI and Oracle moved to let Oracle Cloud customers apply Universal Credits toward OpenAI's frontier models and Codex without opening a new procurement path. Versus yesterday's read that the AI-capex thesis was being repriced through a single hyperscaler-facing supplier's order book, today's is that the labs themselves are now testing both how much equity capital the market will fund and how cleanly that compute sells through incumbent cloud channels.

items.headline: AI events to plan around now - WWDC closes today, Databricks opens Monday, summer tracks span security and chip
items.diff_narrative: Carried forward from 2026-06-11's events bullet across the same three tracks (mainstream developer/data, AI-security, AI-chip/hardware), with date-passed entries dropped and still-upcoming ones held. The clock advances by one day: WWDC26, which yesterday was billed as closing Friday June 12, now reaches its final day today. The mainstream anchors gain detail - Databricks' Data + AI Summit (June 15-18) is now spelled out across Moscone North, West and South with 800-plus sessions and the Chainsmokers at Oracle Park on June 17, and the AI Engineer World's Fair date is corrected to June 29-July 2. The AI-security track adds OWASP Global AppSec USA (November 2-6) and keeps the standing Zenity global-expansion watch; the AI-chip track holds AMD Advancing AI (July 22-23, MI400-series with an MI450 unveil anticipated) and Hot Chips (August 23-25, early registration through July 31), both unchanged from yesterday's firm-ups. GitHub Universe (October 28-29) and AWS re:Invent (November 30-December 4) persist further out.
